title: Failure: The secret to success
content:
1. No one likes to admit failure. The word stands for defeat, disappointment and not being perfect. Rick Newman, the chief business correspondent at U.S. News & World Report, studied 12 successful, well-known people from various professions and determined that they all had something in common: failure.

2. These individuals suffered career setbacks and sometimes a significant blow to their self-confidence, but they all managed to rise above the challenges to achieve greater success than they had ever imagined. Newman calls these individuals "rebounders" and he shares their struggles, hardships and great comebacks in his new book Rebounders: How Winners Pivot from Setback to Success.

3. In an interview, Newman says readers of the book should view setbacks as a process, not defeat. He notes that famous business leaders and scholars recognize that failure cannot be avoided in life and often failure is what makes someone stronger and better able to deal with difficult situations.

4. Newman gives examples of famous people who recovered from misfortune.

5. Thomas Edison failed many times before he changed the world forever. He may best be known for inventing the electric light bulb, phonograph and motion picture camera, but Newman says even Edison created failures. Edison learned from his failed experiments and applied those lessons to future projects.

6. Harry Potter author J. K. Rowling is one of the richest people in Britain. But in the early 1990s she was a single-mother, suffering from depression, and had no money. After countless rejections, one publisher decided to take on her Harry Potter idea. The seven-book series became blockbuster movies, theme parks and one of the most popular book series around the world.

7. Apple founder and former CEO Steve Jobs may be one of the greatest innovators of all time, but even the genius' career hit a low point. Fired from the company he helped to build in 1985, Jobs felt depressed and rejected but directed his energy into new ventures (like Pixar) before returning to Apple in 1996. In his famous 2005 speech at Stanford, Jobs said, "I didn't see it then, but it turned out that getting fired from Apple was the best thing that could have ever happened to me. The heaviness of being successful was replaced by the lightness of being a beginner again, less sure about everything. It freed me to enter one of the most creative periods of my life."

8. Here are Newman's nine key features of a "rebounder":

9. • They accept failure (and can recognize their own mistakes).

10. • They contain their emotions (they won't let themselves be affected by bad feelings).

11. • They prefer action (responding actively to a challenge).

12. • They change their minds sometimes (the need to do away with old thinking and pursue a new dream).

13. • They prepare for things to go wrong (rebounders are not necessarily optimists).

14. • They're comfortable with discomfort (they're willing to accept inconvenience as long as it leads them closer to an important goal).

15. • They're willing to wait (overnight success seldom occurs).

16. • They have heroes (rebounders set and meet higher standards when inspired by others).

17. • They have more than passion (success requires drive, too).

18. Newman says that recovering from failure can be emotionally difficult but adds that failure teaches you important things that can help you a great deal in the future. "You have to keep your mind open," he says. "You have to realize this is just a process, more is coming. And don't be afraid."
